This '''Duel on [[Susevfi]]''' occurred near the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], when a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] strike team traveled to Susevfi and attempted to turn a band of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith cultist/Legends|cultists]] back to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]]. The cultists rebuffed and attacked them. The Jedi [[Death/Legends|slew]] the Sith, but [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Nejaa Halcyon]] was mortally wounded.

==History==
===Prelude===
After the [[Clone Wars/Legends|war between]] the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] began, [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] converted Tyris to his cause with the promise of letting him access a [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocron]] Dooku had stolen from the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]. This [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] had been one that the famous Anzat [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Volfe Karkko]] often accessed.

===The duel===
Some time following the [[Battle of Praesitlyn]], three Jedi found the training camp and the nascent Jensaarai. Nejaa Halcyon, [[Ylenic It'kla]] (who referred to Tyris as '''Nightsweat'''), and one It'kla called "[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Desertwind]]" (actually [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]) attempted to turn the Dark Jedi from their path, but were rebuffed. Attacked, the Jedi squared off against Tyris and his companions and battle was joined. "Desertwind" managed to kill his opponent, the apparent leader of the Jensaarai, and Ylenic slew the Dark Jedi he identified as "[[Dustrose]]."

Halcyon, however, was less fortunate than the others. Tyris took advantage of Halcyon's lack of [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetic]] powers and ran him through. Before succumbing to his injuries, Halcyon drained the energy out of Tyris's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to break every bone in his body, killing him. The release of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] energies at the deaths of the three Jensaarai leaders collapsed the structure where the rest of the Jensaarai were dwelling, killing all but four of the apprentices. The survivors included the [[Unidentified female Saarai-kaar|wife]] of one of Tyris' apprentices, the woman who would later become the [[Saarai-kaar]] of the Jensaarai.

==Aftermath==
After the declaration of the Empire, Obi-Wan Kenobi journeyed to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in order to bring [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to his uncle and aunt. On [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], he encountered Sukarr's daughter, [[Mei (Dark Jedi)|Mei]], who was determined to have her revenge on the man who killed her father.<ref name="Lone Wolf" />

The Saarai-Kaar rebuilt the Jensaarai, but they were unable to comprehend the Sith writings of Larad Noon, and developed practices that only skirted the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] without embracing it. The Jensaarai would eventually become allies with the Jedi Order, and would be considered as [[Gray Jedi]] by the [[New Jedi Order]].
